chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about eating cheese and carrying a sword in which there is glue and tallow, so he said: There is no harm with it, as long as you do not know that it is from a dead animal.

key_terms.الْكَيْمُخْتُ: Glue (specifically animal-based glue used in binding)

ai.seo_question: Is cheese permissible if the glue used in its production comes from a dead animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar illustrates the Shia principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity), where the default permissibility of manufactured goods like cheese and swords is maintained unless specific knowledge of impurity (najis) is established. It highlights the practical legal distinction between the certainty of an animal being dead (maytah) and the uncertainty of whether its byproducts (glue and tallow) were derived from a ritually slaughtered source, a key nuance in Usuli jurisprudence.
